text.p: These are the leading stories in the Lebanese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Lebanon's by-elections: Indifference in the north and a tough battle in Jbeil.
- Saudi Crown Prince Abdullah ended his visit to Lebanon.
- Arab information ministers approve establishing an exhibition on the Qana massacre in which Israel killed about 100 civilians last year in south Lebanon.
- Saudi Crown Prince Abdullah to as-Safir: We will not attend the Doha conference...We are friends with the Americans but we have our politics.

- Former head of Hizbollah Sheikh Tufaili calls on Hizbollah cadres to join his "hunger revolt"; he is calling on residents of the Bekaa Valley to begin a civil disobedience campaign on July 4 to pressure the government into easing poverty in the region.
- Public sector employees allowed to join unions, still banned from staging strikes.
- Prime Minister Hariri plans to stay in Paris during Tufaili's hunger revolt on July 4. Hrawi wants him back in Lebanon before that date.
- Solidere and shares rise on the Beirut Stock Exchange.
